introduction.situation: People design buildings, places and objects so that they can be used for human purposes.
introduction.complication: Sources describe designed arrangements through activity vocabularies, object lists, planning schemes and building schemes that overlap and mix catch-all headings.
introduction.question: How is everything in the field of designed arrangements for human use divided?
introduction.answer: Design's objects divide, from the need to the life of the result, into five aspects of a designed arrangement for human use: use and need, form, performance in use, place and settlement, and the life of the built thing.

governing_thought: Design's objects divide, from the need to the life of the result, into five aspects of a designed arrangement for human use: use and need, form, performance in use, place and settlement, and the life of the built thing.

key_line.mece_dimension: the aspect of a designed arrangement for human use
key_line.rank_note: The aspects run in time from the need that prompts a design to the later life of what is built.

points.title: Use and need
points.statement: Use and need is the aspect in which human activity and purpose call a designed arrangement into being and define the kinds of design.
points.name: Use and need is the aspect in which human activity and purpose call a designed arrangement into being and define the kinds of design.

support.rank_note: The broad framing of activity comes before the particular kinds of design it gives rise to.

points.statement: Framing concepts give the activity vocabulary and the overall field of design within which designed arrangements for human use are studied.
points.name: Framing concepts give the activity vocabulary and the overall field of design within which designed arrangements for human use are studied.

points.statement: Getty hierarchies of activity kinds name the broad classes of human doing, from techniques to events, that a designed arrangement serves.
points.name: Getty hierarchies of activity kinds name the broad classes of human doing, from techniques to events, that a designed arrangement serves.

support.rank_note: Ordered by the position of each hierarchy in the Getty AAT Activities facet.

points.statement: The Activities facet and its general-context term are the overarching Getty labels under which the activity hierarchies sit.
points.name: The Activities facet and its general-context term are the overarching Getty labels under which the activity hierarchies sit.

support.rank_note: Ranked from the most inclusive term, the facet, to the narrower general-context term.

points.statement: Design as a whole field, together with its history, theory and management, frames the study of designed arrangements.
points.name: Design as a whole field, together with its history, theory and management, frames the study of designed arrangements.

support.rank_note: Ordered from the field itself to its reflective and organisational subfields.
Ordered from the specific activity hierarchies to the overarching labels and then the whole field of design.

points.statement: Design subfields are the particular kinds of design distinguished by their practice, their human concern, their medium, or their purpose.
points.name: Design subfields are the particular kinds of design distinguished by their practice, their human concern, their medium, or their purpose.

points.statement: Design subfields centred on making and shaping products, services and experiences for people are the practice-oriented kinds of design.
points.name: Design subfields centred on making and shaping products, services and experiences for people are the practice-oriented kinds of design.

points.statement: Data visualisation and computational (incl. parametric and generative) design
points.name: Data visualisation and computational (incl. parametric and generative) design

support.rank_note: Ranked from the general methods of practice to the most specific design outputs.

points.statement: Design subfields that address human needs, safety and context are the human-centred kinds of design.
points.name: Design subfields that address human needs, safety and context are the human-centred kinds of design.

support.rank_note: Ordered from the human body and culture to hazards and relief situations.

points.statement: Medium-based design fields are defined by the kind of material or artefact they shape for human use, such as cloth, images, or uncategorised products.
points.name: Medium-based design fields are defined by the kind of material or artefact they shape for human use, such as cloth, images, or uncategorised products.

Ordered from practice-oriented and human-centred fields to medium-based and purpose-based fields.

field_check.governing_thought: Design's objects divide, from the need to the life of the result, into five aspects of a designed arrangement for human use: use and need, form, performance in use, place and settlement, and the life of the built thing.
key_line: Use and need is the aspect in which human activity and purpose call a designed arrangement into being and define the kinds of design.
Form is the aspect in which designed arrangements take shape as named kinds of objects, buildings and urban forms.
Performance in use is the aspect in which a designed arrangement works for the people who occupy it, through technical systems and human wellbeing.
Place and settlement is the aspect in which designed arrangements are set within land, regions and communities and governed by plans and rules.
Life of the built thing is the aspect in which a built arrangement is managed, costed, conserved and protected over its existence.
